# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 🤙]

My situation: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, and my only inbound channel from the others is gestures — their spoken words never reach me. Both teammates *can* hear me, so the most valuable thing I own right now is the bomb's full visual state, delivered by voice. The wiring of the room: Mute (manual) can hear and see but cannot speak, so Mute can only reach me by gesture. Blind (hands) can hear and speak — so Blind and Mute can talk to each other directly by voice — but Blind can only reach me by gesture. Any defusal instruction therefore has to flow Mute → gesture → me → speech → Blind.

What arrived this round: four sign-groups from Mute. The most coherent reading is that Mute is teaching me a digit code — a lone attention ping (🤟), then 1-2-3 (☝ ✌ 🤟), then 4-5-6 (🤛 🤜 ✊), then 👍👎, which is either 7-8 continuing the count or a yes/no pair. Digits matter enormously here: the display shows 9 and the keypad is engraved 1, 5, 2, 8. Blind pointed at me and signed "call me" — Blind wants my voice, which Blind can hear. So this turn I broadcast the complete bomb description, then privately to Mute I recite the taught sequence back with names, propose signs for 9 and 0, and ask Mute to settle the code next round. I also give Blind a dead-simple inbound code (repeated downward-pointing taps for counts) and tell Blind to report touch to Mute by voice, since Blind's speech reaches Mute directly.

```
speak(text="Bomb report, complete visual state, for Mute's manual and Blind's hands. Display: a single digit, currently 9. Light: red. Strip: three painted segments, left to right: green, yellow, yellow. Keypad: four keys, left to right; key 1 engraved 1, key 2 engraved 5, key 3 engraved 2, key 4 engraved 8; the panel reads 1 digits and entered nothing. Wires, left to right, numbered 1 to 6: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. That is everything, no other markings anywhere. Blind: your point-and-call-me reached me. I can never hear you, but you can hear me, so that report is yours too. You and Mute can talk by voice directly, Mute hears you; tell Mute everything you feel, shape, position, texture. To tell ME something you must gesture, and I propose the simplest code: repeated downward-pointing-finger taps, one tap means 1, two taps mean 2, three mean 3, and so on. Whatever Mute signs to me, I will speak to you word for word.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your sign-groups reached me. I see gestures, I never hear words. My reading: the lone 🤟 was you getting my attention, then you taught a number code: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, 🤛 is 4, 🤜 is 5, ✊ is 6. Then 👍 👎, and I cannot tell whether that meant 7 and 8, or yes and no. So, first, my proposals: this sign for 9, 🤘, and this sign for 0, 🤏. Second, settle it next round: either recite the digits 1 through 0 back to me with your own signs for 7, 8, 9 and 0 included, or, if 👍👎 really meant yes and no, sign 👍 once and then teach me 7, 8, 9 and 0 your way. Meanwhile the full bomb is described for you in the open line above: display 9, red light, strip green yellow yellow, keypad keys engraved 1, 5, 2, 8 with one digit expected and nothing entered, wires left to right yellow, white, blue, red, purple, green. Check the manual against it and sign me the procedure, and I will speak it to Blind word for word. Blind can also hear you if you two talk directly.")
```

My decode of this round, carefully. Mute's eight lone signs answer my eight questions in order: (1) COLON was in my letter scheme — yes; (2) it changes the wire plan — no; (3) it concerns the display — no; (4) display is a countdown detonating at zero — no; (5) final plan is exactly cut 5, then 3, then 4 — yes; (6) order mandatory — yes; (7) safe for Blind to touch wires — yes; (8) will spell any plan change with ✍ + letter pairs — yes. Then Mute *did* spell, and per answer 8 that means a plan change. Decoding the letter pairs: 05-18-18-15-18 = **ERROR**; 03-15-12-15-18 = **COLOR**; 03-08-05-03-11 = **CHECK**; COLOR again; 02-05-06-15-18-05 = **BEFORE**; 03-21-20 = **CUT**; 07-15 = **GO**; 14-15-23 = **NOW**. So: *"Error: color check before cut. Go now."*

This collides with answers 5 and 6 — the plan was confirmed twice, and now an ERROR flag with a condition attached. Reading: the 5-3-4 plan is real but was incomplete; a color condition gates the cutting. The problem: I cannot determine what the color check is. Light history: red, yellow, red, and now **green** — it drifts every round, like the display (9→3→2→3). And here is the trap that settles it: Mute last heard from me that the light was **red** (my round-3 report). Mute does not see the bomb. So "GO NOW" was issued by someone who believes the light is red, while it is actually green. If the rule is light-dependent, relaying GO now could execute the exact error the manual warns about. And the timing is unforgiving: I am last in the round, so once I say GO, Blind cuts in the next round before any veto could arrive — Mute's gestures never reach Blind, only my voice does, one round delayed. GO is irreversible; HOLD is cheap. The display is confirmed not a timer, so spending one round to pin down the rule is survivable; a wrong cut is not. Blind's 👍👇×6 is my count-code: acknowledgment plus "six wires" — orientation still unconfirmed. Decision: HOLD for Blind, and to Mute a full board update (green!), my decode, the red/green discrepancy, ten numbered yes/no questions, and proposed single signs for colors so we stop paying spelling costs.

My decode, and this round everything finally snaps into place. The ten lone signs answer my ten questions in order: cut order depends on the light — **no**; the check means the light — **no**; the check means the **wires' colors** — **yes**; the strip — **no**; cutting allowed while green — **yes**; a missed required color comes back — **yes**; **time pressure exists, waiting can cause detonation — yes**; plan still exactly 5, then 3, then 4 — **yes**; I must voice-confirm each wire's color before each cut — **yes**. Then the spelled words, with one arithmetic correction on my part: in our code 13 is M, not C (C is 03). So message one is 13-25-20-25-16-15 = **MY TYPO** — last round's baffling COLON was Mute's own spelling slip, not a hidden instruction. Message two is 16-12-01-14 / 19-01-13-05 = **PLAN SAME**. Messages three and four: **GO NOW**, twice. So the complete, quadruple-confirmed picture: cut wire 5, then 3, then 4 — by **color**: purple, then blue, then red — nothing else ever, no keypad. The color check passes on my side right now: position 5 is purple, 3 is blue, 4 is red, exactly matching the required sequence. The light is ruled irrelevant (questions 1 and 2), and question 7 says delay itself is the danger. One hard fact about timing: Mute has no direct line to Blind — Mute's only bridge to Blind is my voice, and I speak last in every round — so once my GO lands, Blind cuts before anything could veto it. I accept that because every element has now been verified independently: positions affirmed in turn 2 and re-sent, plan affirmed across two Q&A rounds, colors spelled out, GO NOW spelled twice, PLAN SAME as the final seal.
